description: How AI systems read this blog: reads by signal type over the last 7 days (Pro: 30 or 90), next to the equal period before. Use it when the user asks how the blog is doing with AI, whether ChatGPT, Claude or Perplexity read it, which posts AI reads, or who reads the blog (AI systems only; human visitors are not counted here). Four tiers, strongest signal first. `click`: a reader followed a link to the blog from an AI assistant's answer. `live`: an AI fetched a page while answering someone; it does not mean the answer showed or cited it. `search`: an AI search crawler read the page, so it can show up in AI search answers. `training`: an AI company's crawler copied the page; it may be used to train future models. Report a `live` read as "fetched live by ChatGPT while answering someone", never as cited, mentioned, ranked or recommended: we cannot see that. Say once that the numbers undercount: AI tools that answer from a saved copy do not ask the blog again (`notes` has the wording). `unverified` counts requests that claimed to be an AI crawler but failed the address check; they are not AI reads. Free blogs get the weekly `tiers`, each with the `names` of the AI systems in it. Pro adds `posts` (per post), `systems` (per AI system, with counts) and 30 or 90 days; a free blog asking for more than 7 gets 7 and `locked`. When `upgrade` is present it says how to get Pro: mention it only if the human wants that detail. Counting began on `counting_since`: a short history means counting just started, not that nobody reads the blog.

blog_id.description: Your blog's id, as returned by signup. Optional with an API key: it defaults to the key's blog, and any id you pass must be that blog. Required when the server runs without API keys.

days.description: Window in days, ending today (UTC): 7 (default), 30 or 90. A free blog always gets 7 and a `locked` list.
